change_interpretations.engineering_summary: The response time limit for driver torque requests above 70% pedal demand was tightened from 100 ms to 80 ms. Verification procedures, script thresholds, and past test evidence must be re-evaluated against the 80 ms limit.

assessments.reason: TV-001 directly tests VCU-DR-01 with a procedure and script threshold of 100 ms. The previous pass result of 94 ms fails the new 80 ms limit, invalidating previous evidence and procedure parameters.
assessments.recommended_action: Update the procedure and test script threshold to 80 ms and re-run TV-001 on the bench.

assessments.reason: TV-002 applies 85% pedal demand and links to VCU-DR-01, but previous evidence recorded no timing data. It is unknown whether the torque command response met the new 80 ms threshold.
evidence: Comment: Timing not reported in old evidence
assessments.recommended_action: Re-run TV-002 with timing capture to measure response latency against the 80 ms limit.

assessments.reason: TV-003 measures torque response time for pedal sweeps between 75% and 95% demand. The recorded maximum of 92 ms and script tolerance of 95 ms fail the updated 80 ms limit of VCU-DR-01.
evidence: Comment: Legacy suite still checks 95 ms tolerance
Workshop note: High-load campaign did not keep all requirement hyperlinks after migration
assessments.recommended_action: Restore the requirement link to VCU-DR-01, update script tolerance to 80 ms, and re-test TV-003.

assessments.reason: TV-004 verifies emergency brake command latency under VCU-BRK-03. Workshop notes explicitly state that brake latency uses a different measurement clock from torque latency and must not be conflated.
evidence: Workshop note: Brake command latency and positive torque command latency are measured by different clocks
assessments.recommended_action: Retain existing test procedure and evidence for TV-004 without modification.

assessments.reason: TV-005 tests wheel-speed sensor fault detection and degraded mode logging under unchanged requirement VCU-DGN-04, which is unrelated to driver torque response timing.
evidence: Procedure: Unplug simulated wheel-speed sensor and confirm degraded mode + fault log

assessments.reason: TV-006 verifies audit logging for operating mode changes under unchanged requirement VCU-LOG-05, having no impact from VCU-DR-01 changes.
evidence: Procedure: Change Comfort to Sport; log timestamp and build identifier

assessments.reason: TV-007 exercises 80% pedal demand but has a TBD requirement link, unclear ownership, and has never been run, breaking traceability.
evidence: Comment: Ownership and source link to be clarified
assessments.recommended_action: Request test owner clarification to resolve the TBD link and confirm applicability of VCU-DR-01.

assessments.reason: TV-008 references an unknown requirement VCU-OLD-88 from a legacy tracker, resulting in broken traceability that prevents determining relevance to specification changes.
evidence: Comment: Imported row; requirements catalog changed
assessments.recommended_action: Review legacy mapping with the system engineer to re-link or retire TV-008.

assessments.reason: TV-009 compares accelerator torque ramps between Sport and Comfort modes without quantitative response-time assertions. Mode-specific torque ramp profiles may plausibly affect compliance with VCU-DR-01.
evidence: Procedure: Compare accelerator response under Sport vs Comfort
assessments.recommended_action: Re-evaluate TV-009 to determine whether quantitative response-time measurement against VCU-DR-01 should be added.

assessments.reason: TV-010 tests transient pedal signal spike filtering under unchanged requirement VCU-DR-02, verifying signal rejection rather than high-demand torque response latency.
evidence: Procedure: Inject 7 ms false pedal pulse

assessments.reason: TV-011 verifies emergency brake override priority over positive torque under unchanged requirement VCU-BRK-03, which does not measure driver torque response time.
evidence: Procedure: verify positive torque drops according to brake priority

assessments.reason: TV-012 measures ECU power-cycle wake-up readiness time, which is a platform startup function completely unrelated to driver torque response VCU-DR-01.
evidence: Procedure: Power cycle the ECU; verify readiness within 500 ms
assessments.recommended_action: No action required regarding VCU-DR-01; optionally assign a platform requirement link.
